title: Marcus Dupree's 239 Yards in the 1983 Fiesta Bowl
question: How many yards did Marcus Dupree rush for in the 1983 Fiesta Bowl?
answer: Oklahoma freshman Marcus Dupree ran 17 times for 239 yards against Arizona State on January 1, 1983, a Fiesta Bowl rushing record. The Sooners still lost 32-21.
summary: Freshman Marcus Dupree ran for 239 yards on 17 carries in the 1983 Fiesta Bowl, a game record, though Oklahoma fell 32-21 to Arizona State in Tempe.
body: Marcus Dupree arrived in Norman in 1982 as one of the most talked-about recruits in the country, a 6-foot-3, roughly 228-pound back out of Philadelphia, Mississippi. His start was quiet. Running the wishbone, he gained only 20 yards in Oklahoma's first three games, and the Sooners opened 1-2.

Barry Switzer and his staff changed course after a scrimmage in which Dupree carried six times for 158 yards. They moved the offense into an I formation, and the freshman took off. By the end of the regular season he had 905 rushing yards, an Oklahoma freshman record at that point, and Oklahoma won seven straight before a loss to Nebraska left the team 8-3.

The Sooners then met Arizona State in the Fiesta Bowl on New Year's Day 1983 at Sun Devil Stadium in Tempe, in front of 70,553 fans. Dupree gave fans their most vivid look at what he could do. He carried 17 times for 239 yards, a 14.1-yard average with a longest run of 56 yards, and he was named the game's offensive player. The 239 yards set a Fiesta Bowl rushing record.

He did it while battling injuries and he left in the third quarter with a pulled hamstring. Oklahoma ran for 417 yards as a team, yet Arizona State won 32-21, helped by a 54-yard field goal from Luis Zendejas as the first half expired, another Fiesta Bowl record.
It remains one of the great individual days in Sooner bowl history, and a reminder of how much promise fans saw in a freshman who was only getting started.
